request.state: CanLang authors business declarations in .can source. The user now requests an internal developer/integrator reference and questions whether translated declaration descriptions earn their authoring cost. Existing # prose attaches to declarations. Scenario prose is shown in IDE hover using its source text; scenario metadata retains translations, but published MCP operation descriptors copy only the source string. Field input descriptions currently accept literal @{desc="..."} and remain plain strings. Localized page descriptions already have a browser consumer. Source-string message parsing, message IR and locale formatters exist, but there is no can documentation command in the inspected CLI. The proposed inline field spelling is desc="Source"@{nl="Translation"}. Neither that spelling nor localized MCP field output is implemented. The user selected an internal developer and integrator audience for the first documentation version. Required outcomes: accurate source-derived reference, minimal repetitive source, unchanged business types/authority, and honest support claims. A documentation generator must not invent effects, infer executable permissions from prose, or pretend displayed examples passed. Removing description variants would leave actual UI captions/messages localized. No multilingual reference readership has been established. This is a design choice, not a measured implementation or performance result.

description_policy.instructions: For the requested internal reference, which policy best balances useful documentation, optional multilingual readership, implementation scope and concise authoring? Judge all options under the same fidelity and audience constraints.

criteria.source_only: Generate a deterministic internal reference from declarations and source-language descriptions. Remove localization support for declaration descriptions, while preserving localization of actual UI captions/messages/pages. Low translation maintenance and simpler metadata; multilingual reference readers receive source-language prose.
criteria.optional_shared: Generate the same deterministic internal reference and keep declaration-description translations optional. Inline desc= and attached # use one static description value. Explicit documentation locale uses shared fallback, and MCP can reuse that value at its own metadata boundary. Never require a translation merely because syntax allows one. Adds metadata plumbing and locale tests; actual multilingual use justifies each translated asset.
criteria.ai_first: Generate the internal reference using an AI documentation writer grounded in declaration facts and source descriptions. Produce reviewable source-cited prose and translated drafts only after review; retain real UI localization. More explanatory workflow guidance is possible, with model cost, nondeterminism and factual-review obligations. No generated prose is executable or accepted as test evidence.
